title: QBR Token Forecast & Renewal Scenario Planner
body:
Purpose:
This is a working planner for QBRs that combines short-term token forecasts with renewal / capacity scenarios. Goal: give CSMs and FinOps clear, repeatable scenarios (baseline, moderate growth, spike) plus specific rate-limit and budget alert prescriptions to surface to customers and internal teams ahead of renewal conversations.

Scope and audience:
- Primary: CSMs prepping QBRs with mid-market and enterprise customers on hosted API and dedicated plans.
- Secondary: Solutions Engineering and Customer FinOps who run runway calculations and recommend Dedicated sizing.
- Not included: in-depth infra-level capacity planning for Private installs (those use separate infra runbooks).

Quick summary (one-liner):
Provide 3 forward-looking token scenarios for the next 90 days + recommended guardrails (alert thresholds, soft throttles, escalation paths) to reduce renewal risk and unexpected billing spikes.

Data inputs (minimum):
- trailing 30/60/90 day token consumption by route and model version (hourly granularity ideally)
- peak 1-hour and 1-day token bursts in last 90 days
- customer SLA tier and rate-limit config/limits
- committed spend / reserved capacity details (if any)
- key workflows: background batch jobs vs interactive user traffic vs async pipelines
- known upcoming events (marketing campaigns, product launches, migrations)

Forecast methodology (simple, repeatable):
1) Baseline: rolling 30-day average scaled to 90 days.
2) Growth: baseline * (1.2 – 3.0) depending on account signals (sales pipeline, product calendar). Use explicit multiplier and justify with attached evidence.
3) Spike: project a short-duration multiplier (5x–15x) applied to peak-day observed or estimated promotional traffic. Build both best-guess and worst-case columns.
4) Renewal hit: compute delta between forecasted 90-day consumption and committed capacity / committed spend. Flag where delta > 15% (risk) and > 50% (critical).

Example scenario table (paste into QBR slides / worksheet):

Scenario | Avg daily tokens | 90d total tokens | Est billing delta vs commit | Notes
---------|------------------|------------------|---------------------------|------
Baseline | 120,000         | 10,800,000       | +0% (within commit)       | Normal usage, no campaigns
Growth (1.8x)| 216,000      | 19,440,000       | +80% -> recommend partial reserved increase or budget alert cadence
Spike (5x peak 2d)| 600,000 (2d peak)| 25,200,000| +133% -> recommend temporary burst protection + throttles

Budget impact calc (simple):
- Pricing assumptions: hosted per-token unit price = $0.0006 (example).
- 90d cost = tokens * unit price.
- Delta cost = (forecast_tokens - commit_tokens) * unit price.
- If delta cost > customer monthly budget * 0.2, flag for finance consult.

Recommended proactive controls (order of preference):
1) Soft budget alerts (email + Slack): at 50%, 75%, 90% of monthly budget. Include projected burn date.
2) Per-route throttles: set conservative limits for non-critical batch routes (e.g., nightly indexing) that can be backfilled.
3) Burst protection policy: temporary caps with auto-rolloff (24–72h) and manual override.
4) Canary fallback model: route to smaller/quantized model variant when latency/cost SLOs exceed threshold.
5) Reservation recommendation: suggest reserved capacity or commit level if forecasted steady-state > 70% of commit for 60+ days.

Practical alert thresholds (example values to adapt per customer):
- Token burn: 50% of monthly budget -> "heads up" email to both CSM and FinOps
- Token burn: 75% -> schedule quick health sync (15m) and run a bill impact slide for QBR
- Token burn: 90% -> auto-create escalation ticket; enable soft throttle if agreed in contract
- Sustained hourly QPS above 3x baseline for 6 hours -> trigger SRE engagement

Sample Slack alert message (short):
"[CS ALERT] AcmeCorp has hit 75% of monthly token budget (projected exhaustion in 6 days). Recommend brief sync before next marketing email. CSM: Aisha P., FinOps: Marco R."

Rate-limit playbook (actionable):
- If 50%: notify, confirm known events, confirm non-critical jobs can slow down.
- If 75%: run partial throttle on non-interactive routes, tag for QBR discussion and suggest immediate 7-day reserved bump (if on Dedicated).
- If 90%: apply agreed contract throttles or soft-block; run live bill projection with finance; prepare renewal negotiation briefing.

Renewal scenarios and recommended CSM narrative (short templates):
1) Healthy renewal (baseline or small growth): "Usage steady; recommend same commit with small 10-20% cushion; propose Optimize review for batching improvements."
2) Upsell (sustained growth): "Customer will exceed commit by X% on current trajectory; propose tiered reserved package with per-month smoothing and a 30% discount on commit for a 12-month term."
3) At-risk (spike / budget overrun): "Immediate short-term mitigation steps applied (throttles/alerts). Need to align on mitigation and budget increase before renewal to avoid churn. Suggest 90-day temporary burst add-on."

QBR talking points and artifacts to bring:
- One-slide summary: 3-scenario table + delta vs commit + recommended ask (e.g., add 20% to commit or enable 2-week burst allowance).
- Timeline: when support was engaged, what throttles were applied, and any service degradation notes.
- Metrics: peak QPS, top 3 routes by token volume, average token size per request, estimated cost per route.
- Action list with owners and due dates.

Runbook: Alerts -> Triage -> Action -> Follow-up
- Triage owner: on-call CSM / CS FinOps (first responder)
- Immediate action: check top-5 routes, confirm any scheduled jobs, assess atypical or external drivers (campaigns).
- Mitigation actions: schedule throttles, enable burst caps, contact engineering if model fallback needed.
- Follow-up: update ticket, add to QBR artifacts, recommend renewal adjustments if needed.

Open questions / data gaps (fill before QBR):
- Do we have hourly histogram for token sizes per route for last 90 days? (critical for spike sims)
- Are there externally scheduled events we are unaware of for the next 90 days? (marketing/product)
- What is the exact contract language around soft throttles vs hard blocks for this account?
- Any pending model upgrades or migration that will change per-token cost?

Next steps / checklist for CSM before QBR (editable):
- [ ] Pull 30/60/90 day token CSV by route + model version
- [ ] Run the 3-scenario calculator (this doc) and paste table into slide deck
- [ ] Validate planned product/marketing events with customer PMs
- [ ] Confirm commit details with Billing/Finance
- [ ] If forecast shows >15% delta: propose 1:1 pre-QBR customer conversation
- [ ] Draft renewal narrative and recommended contract amendment (if needed)

Owners and escalation contacts:
- CSM: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai)
- CS FinOps: Marco Ruiz (marco@redwood.ai)
- Solutions Eng: Dana Kim (dana@redwood.ai)
- On-call SRE/Serving Runtime: rotation list in PagerDuty (see Confluence link)

Notes / rough thoughts (working doc):
- Consider adding a small "cost-per-conversation" metric for chat-heavy customers that use function-calling heavily — it helps translate tokens to dollars for execs.
- For Dedicated customers, model fallback recommendations should include expected latency delta when moving to smaller quantized models.
- We should add a simple Google Sheets template that auto-calculates the scenario table when the CSM pastes the three numbers. Tagging as action item for Dana.

End of planner. This is intentionally lightweight and prescriptive — meant to be copy-pasted into a QBR slide and used in a pre-QBR risk call. Keep it updated with real unit pricing and customer commit details before finalizing slides.
